title: DAG layout: ready_vs_open_based_on_blockers test fails on main
description:
Pre-existing failure on main (commit 8363e97, v1.5.1), discovered while working on wt-exo.

worktree-dash-rs/src/ui/dag_graph/layout.rs:553
assertion failed: expected CardStatus::Open, got CardStatus::Blocked

Reproduction: git stash on a clean tree, cargo test ready_vs_open — fails.

Test setup (layout.rs:541-555):
- task 'a' closed, no blockers
- task 'b' open, blocker=['a']  → expected Ready (and passes)
- task 'c' open, no blockers
- task 'd' open, blocker=['c']  → expected Open, actually Blocked

title: DAG progress bar: renderer + wire into render_graph
description:
Implement draw_progress_bar(area, buf, layout) in worktree-dash-rs/src/ui/dag_graph/render.rs.

Spec:
- Bar width: 30 cells
- Position: y = area.y + area.height - 1 (the pad row minimap and legends both leave empty)
- x = area.x + (area.width - 30) / 2 (horizontally centered)
- Glyph: █ in each bucket's existing status color (Done=Green, Ready=Cyan, Active=Yellow, Blocked=Red)
- Inline 'NN%' painted centered over each segment when that segment is ≥4 cells wide; smaller segments unlabeled
- Label fg: contrasting (black or HEADER_BG) against the colored block
- Skip fallback: if area.width < 34 or area too short, return early (same pattern as draw_minimap)
- Empty layout: return early

Call site: inside the existing 'if state.overlays_visible' block in render_graph (render.rs ~L141), right after draw_minimap. No new key handler needed — Ctrl+G already toggles overlays_visible.

title: DAG progress bar: bucket counting + segment allocation helpers
description:
Add pure helpers in worktree-dash-rs/src/ui/dag_graph/render.rs:

- fn bucket_counts(cards: &[Card]) -> [usize; 4]
  Folds 5 CardStatus variants into 4 buckets: [DONE, READY_OPEN, ACTIVE, BLOCKED]
  Mapping: Done→0, Ready|Open→1, Active→2, Blocked→3

- fn allocate_segments(counts: [usize; 4], bar_w: usize) -> [Segment; 4]
  Largest-remainder rounding for BOTH percentages (sum == 100) and widths (sum == bar_w).
  Nonzero buckets that round to 0 cells get a forced minimum of 1 cell (steal from largest bucket).
  Zero-count buckets get exactly 0 cells.

- Unit tests covering: empty input, single-bucket, equal split, odd totals, zero-count mix, min-1-cell enforcement, widths-sum-to-bar_w across many inputs, pcts-sum-to-100.
close_reason: helpers + 11 unit tests passing; no new clippy warnings

title: Test task with long description for scroll testing
description:
This is a very long description to test scrolling in the task detail view. It should wrap across multiple lines and allow the user to scroll up and down to read the full content.

## Requirements
- The task detail panel should show this text with proper word wrapping
- Scrolling with arrow keys or j/k should work smoothly
- The scroll position should be preserved when switching between tasks
- Long paragraphs should break at word boundaries, not in the middle of words

## Technical Details
This description contains multiple paragraphs to test how the panel handles different sections of text. Each paragraph should be separated by a blank line, and the rendering should respect these line breaks.

The implementation uses a manual word-wrap algorithm that breaks at space characters and falls back to character-level breaking when no spaces are found within the available width.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Text wraps correctly at panel width
2. Scroll up/down works with arrow keys
3. Left and right padding is visible (1 char each side)
4. Title also wraps if longer than available width
5. Labels and status are visible below the description
6. Esc returns to the task list view

- cd worktree-dash-rs && cargo test

- Open DAG tab, confirm progress bar appears at bottom-middle

- Ctrl+G toggles bar OFF along with minimap and legends
- Ctrl+G toggles bar back ON

title: Click-drag empty graph area to pan the viewport
description: When the user presses the left button on empty graph area (not on a card) and drags, pan the viewport in the opposite direction of the drag (grab-and-drag feel). Equivalent to h/j/k/l panning but continuous. Store the drag anchor (col, row, vx0, vy0) on DagGraphState when the press lands on empty area; update viewport from the delta on each Drag event; clear the anchor on Up. Clicks with zero drag distance do nothing (no threshold, no deselect).
close_reason: Left press on empty graph area records PanDrag anchor; Drag updates viewport = (vx0 - dx, vy0 - dy) for grab-and-drag feel; Up clears anchor. Clicks with zero drag leave viewport alone.

close_reason: Added overlays_visible: bool (default true) to DagGraphState, manual Default impl. Ctrl+G in the widget-tab key handler toggles it. render_graph skips draw_legends + draw_minimap when false. Documented in help overlay next to h/j/k/l pan.

title: Deselect only on click-without-drag on empty DAG area
description: Currently a left press on empty graph area deselects (hides the tooltip, drops the task list highlight) AND arms pan-drag in one go. So if the user wanted to drag the canvas, the tooltip disappears mid-drag. Fix: keep the tooltip during a drag. Only deselect when the user clicks without moving, which we now detect on Up after no Drag event fired. Implementation: add a moved: bool to PanDrag, flip it in Drag, on Up check !moved and then clear selected_id and tasks_selected.
close_reason: Added moved: bool to PanDrag. Down arms but does not deselect; Drag flips moved; Up deselects only when the drag didn't move, keeping the tooltip visible through a pan.
